reason: The LED half lands at level 0 as the cold comparison in light-bulb-hot-wire; the laser half is university material and belongs to the level-3 physics lens (its 'lasers' proposal), not to this lens.

Not among this lens's thirty: the everyday heat pump is the fridge, which the household-mechanisms lens proposes as refrigerator-heat-mover (heat moved, not made, with the back of the fridge warm); a heating heat pump is the same page run backwards and can be one step of it.

Not a level-0 topic as named. Its everyday faces are spread over this lens's submarine-ballast-tanks (buoyancy), parachute-terminal-speed (drag), kite-string-wind and sailing-into-wind (lift); the subject itself is the level-3 physics lens's navier-stokes proposal.

A level-3 physics topic that belongs to another lens; three level-0 pages here (floating-sinking-and-boats, air-pressure-and-straws, water-pressure-and-hydraulics) are its on-ramp, so keep it as a level-3 candidate rather than fold it into any of them.
Level-3 physics, outside this level-0 lens; glowing-hot is the level-0 contrast (light from heat) that a lasers-and-LEDs page (light without heat) would pick up.
An energy-category topic (level 2) for another lens; keeping-things-warm and temperature-and-touch are the level-0 pages a heat-pump page can assume readers have met.

Promoted at level 3 as a lattice-Boltzmann page swept through the Reynolds number, with turbulence-cascade as a companion; flight already covers the wing, so the new page is the equation itself and the transition to turbulence.

Promoted at level 3 as the rate-equation model of a laser (inversion, threshold, Q-switching); the LED half is a p-n junction run as a light source and belongs as a sentence in semiconductors or solar-cells, not a page of its own.

Honest at level 1 and fills a gap the catalogue leans on without naming it (radioactivity, epidemics, acids-bases and earthquakes all use exponentials or log scales). Narrowed to the rule itself and the logarithm as a count of steps so it does not repeat those pages.

Promoted as a level-3 page on the phase plane, stability and linearization, which no existing page covers; the solver side of the subject goes to the separate numerical-stability candidate rather than one overloaded page.

Promoted at level 3 with replicator dynamics so that the graphic is a real model (an ODE on the simplex) rather than a payoff table to read; Nash equilibria, cycling and spatial cooperation are all observable in it.

Honest at level 1, needs no data, and is one of the strongest-demand interactive topics in mathematics; it also gives the site a second level-1 mathematics page in this batch, which the new-100 plan wants.

Not a level-0 page: it needs light-optics, so it belongs to the level-1 space lens (aperture and light-gathering, why a bigger mirror sees fainter and sharper). Worth promoting there; none of the thirty candidates here replaces it.

Conway's Life is the one cellular automaton a nine-year-old can run by counting neighbours, and the Numberphile demand signal is strong; the deeper material (Wolfram's rules, universality) stays out of this lens and can be added at level 2 or 3 later.

The doubling half (rice on a chessboard, paper folding, add-the-same against double) is level-0 material and lands in growing-patterns; the logarithm half is not level 0 and belongs to a level-1 or level-2 lens, so the Reserve line should stay for that half.

The level-0 page covers the ear's path from eardrum to the place-by-pitch map, which is what a beginner needs; the cochlea's own mechanics (travelling wave, active amplifier, otoacoustic emissions) remain open for a level-3 page under another lens and are not duplicated here.

The household half of the reserve item (a loop that carries heat from cold to warm, and why the back of a fridge is warm) becomes the level-0 refrigerator page. A level-2 heat-pumps page (coefficient of performance against outdoor temperature, the reversing valve, heating a house) is a different page and stays open for the level-2/3 lens.
